title: Database engine comparison
goal: An architecture team can compare database engines for a multi-tenant SaaS.

rubric.must: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and DynamoDB are visibly compared in columns.
Transaction, schema, joins, and serverless criteria are visible as rows.
Yes, no, and partial capabilities are visually distinguishable.
The matrix grid enables row-by-row comparison.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the comparison/matrix exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target visibly presents a readable comparison matrix with three engine columns and four criteria rows. Green checks, amber partial marks, and red crosses distinguish the capability levels; alternating row shading keeps comparisons traceable. No material overlap or cropping is visible.

items.evidence: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and DynamoDB appear as separate column headers.
Rows show ACID transactions, flexible schema, complex joins, and managed serverless option.
Green check, amber partial mark, and red cross are distinct and explained by the Yes/Partly/No legend.
Each criterion forms a row aligned with capability marks under each engine column.
All headings, row labels, and legend labels are readable, with no visible clipping.
